prompt: Build a five-check data-quality report on the raw tables. These tables may hold errors. Return one row for each check, with three columns, in this order: check_name, n_bad and result, 'pass' when n_bad is 0, otherwise 'fail'. The checks and what each counts: 'resent_copies', the order lines that are resent copies (two lines are copies of one order line when order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id and line_discount_eur all match, with a missing promo_id matching a missing one; every line beyond the first of such a set is a resent copy); 'price_in_cents', the order lines whose unit_price_eur is more than 10 times the product's unit_cost_eur; 'sku_not_standard', the products whose sku is not upper case with no spaces at its start or end; 'missing_category', the products with a missing category_id; 'overlapping_prices', the products with two price windows that share at least one day (a window runs from valid_from to valid_to, both days included, and a missing valid_to means the window is still open). Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write one count per check and stack them with UNION ALL in a named step.
Give each check its own SELECT with the rule from the question, the same two columns in each; a CASE on n_bad then gives pass or fail.
why_this_works: Each check counts its own rule in one row, so the report shows how big each problem is, and any count above 0 fails.
